passage:
Sonali, you asked why I deleted my "goals" folder. So, I'm Mehak, and for six months I followed all these gym and makeup creators, and every morning I felt I had to change something: my hair, my stomach, my skin. I bought things I didn't need.
Then one night I watched one of them pitch a "transformation plan", her discount code flashing in the same breath as telling us how much we needed fixing. I thought: who earns when I feel inadequate? She does.
So I unfollowed most of them. Now I follow a swimming coach who posts drills and a science teacher who explains how things work. My mornings are quieter. I still notice myself comparing sometimes, but now I ask who is selling what.

qa.q: What flashed on screen with the influencer's transformation plan?
qa.a: Her discount code flashed on screen in the same breath as the plan.

qa.q: What was Mehak feeling every morning while following the influencers?
qa.a: She felt she had to change something, like her hair, stomach or skin, which suggests envy and a sense of not being enough.

qa.q: What did Mehak change about whom she follows, and why?
qa.a: She unfollowed most of them after asking who earns when she feels inadequate, and now picks accounts that teach real things. 😊

qa.q: How might the influencer see her transformation plan?
qa.a: She may see it as a product and her followers as customers, so she benefits when viewers feel they need fixing.

grounding: Shows a teen envying fitness and beauty influencers, asking who benefits from her inadequacy and choosing accounts for evidence and wellbeing.

passage:
Sunday, late. Spent two hours watching that fitness guy with the eight-pack again. Every reel ends the same way: 'Want this body? Link in bio, special discount on my shred plan.' I kept looking at my own arms and feeling like a flat tyre. I even asked Mum for money for his plan. Then Rafiq said something at cricket that stuck: 'The man earns every time you feel bad about yourself.' Tonight I checked. Every single post sells something: powder, plan, gloves, a 'secret' app. He needs me to feel not enough. So I tried an experiment. Unfollowed him and four others like him. Followed the sports physio our coach recommends, who posts about sleep, warm-ups and injuries and never shows off a stomach. Weird, but I feel calmer already. Still a bit jealous of those arms, honestly. But I'm not paying to feel worse.
- Pranav

qa.q: How does every reel from the fitness influencer end?
qa.a: With an offer: 'Want this body? Link in bio', and a discount on his shred plan.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling while watching those arms in the reels?
qa.a: Pranav felt envious and inadequate, 'like a flat tyre', and still admits to being a bit jealous.

qa.q: Which choice worked for Pranav, and why?
qa.a: Unfollowing accounts that profit from insecurity and following an evidence-based physio, which already left Pranav calmer 🙂

qa.q: How might the influencer see Pranav's feeling of not being enough?
qa.a: As a sales opportunity: every time a viewer feels inadequate, the influencer earns from plans and powders.

grounding: A diary showing a teen envying fitness influencers, checking who profits from that feeling of inadequacy, and choosing evidence-based accounts.

passage:
Minakshi: have you seen Glowwithme's new video?? 12-step glass skin routine
Ojas: the one with the ring light?
Minakshi: her skin literally has no pores. mine looks like a strawberry next to it 😔
Minakshi: I need all 12 products. like, NEED
Ojas: ok but who sent her the 12 products
Minakshi: ...the companies. it says #ad at the bottom
Ojas: so she gets paid when you feel like a strawberry
Minakshi: wow ok rude but true
Ojas: my cousin follows a skin doctor who posts actual studies. no filter, shows her own breakouts
Minakshi: send
Ojas: sent. she says most people need way fewer products than these routines claim
Minakshi: unfollowed glowwithme. followed the doctor. still want that skin tbh
Ojas: fair. but real skin is allowed to have pores 🙂
Minakshi: putting that on my mirror

qa.q: What did it say at the bottom of the influencer's video?
What was Minakshi feeling when making the strawberry comparison?
qa.a: Minakshi felt envious and insecure, sure that all twelve products were needed to fix something wrong.

qa.q: What question helped Minakshi rethink the routine?
qa.a: Ojas asking who sent the products, which showed the influencer gains when viewers feel inadequate.

qa.q: How does Ojas see the glass skin video?
qa.a: Ojas sees it as paid advertising and wants Minakshi to remember that real skin has pores.

grounding: Shows a teen envying a beauty influencer, noticing who benefits from that insecurity, and choosing an evidence-based account instead.
